holidays.name: International Sloth Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the world's slowest, snuggliest tree-dwellers. Fans celebrate by learning about sloths, sharing sloth photos, supporting conservation groups, and taking life at a delightfully slow pace. Napping is encouraged.
holidays.origin: International Sloth Day is held every October 20. It grew out of sloth conservation and awareness efforts, and it is tied to the first International Meeting on Sloth Well-being and Conservation. Groups such as the Sloth Conservation Foundation now use the day to promote protection of sloths and their rainforest homes.
holidays.funFact: Sloths move so slowly that algae grows in their fur, which gives them a faint greenish tint that helps them blend into the treetops.

holidays.name: National Brandied Fruit Day
holidays.description: A day for fruit that has been soaked in brandy and sugar until it turns rich, boozy, and spoon-ready. Spoon it over ice cream, pound cake, or pancakes. You can also use it to start your holiday dessert plans early.
holidays.origin: The day is an unofficial food observance held each October 20. It celebrates the old European practice of preserving fruit in spirits, which dates back to at least the 17th century.
holidays.funFact: Some cooks keep a brandied fruit starter going for months or even years. They top it up with fresh fruit and sugar as they use it.

holidays.name: International Chefs Day
holidays.description: A salute to the cooks who make our meals happen, from restaurant pros to the person who rescues dinner at home. It's a good day to thank a chef, try a new recipe, or at least learn where the spatula lives.
holidays.origin: International Chefs Day is observed every October 20. It was created to celebrate chefs and to encourage healthy eating and food education for younger generations.
holidays.funFact: The tall white chef's hat, called a toque, is traditionally said to have around 100 pleats, representing the many ways a chef can cook an egg.
